title: Design System: LM · Esquadrias, Vidros e Construção

display.purpose: Page h1 only, one per surface. Per-surface clamp, capped at 12-14ch, text-wrap: balance.

display-serif.purpose: Instrument Serif. One number or date per page, maximum. Never a heading, never prose.

headline.purpose: Band titles (h2) on the newer surfaces, clamped. Capped at 15-19ch.

headline-sm.purpose: The smaller band title used by Sobre's historia/equipe/CTA and Localizacao's visita.

headline-fixed.purpose: The home bands' older register: 44/42/40px pinned, stepping to 38px then 34px. Use the clamp on new bands.

title.purpose: Card names, capability headings, the spec panel title.

title-sm.purpose: Recommendation and project card names inside a tighter grid.

body.purpose: Leads and prose, Cinza Texto on paper or white at 64-70% on ink. Always capped by a ch measure.

body-lg.purpose: The opening lead on Sobre and the grupo band.

body-sm.purpose: Card descriptions, notes, breadcrumb links, footnotes.

control.purpose: Button and nav-link type. 14px/650, never uppercase.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, dt in a data list, sidebar legends, footer group titles. Uppercase, tracked open.

micro.purpose: Card footers, counts, badges, stat labels. Never for anything a visitor must read to act.

numeral.purpose: The large tabular step number in the home process glass tiles.

price.purpose: The product page's investment figure. Tabular numerals.

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: Resting state of every card on paper. A seat, not a lift.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover on a catalogue card, paired with translateY(-5px). The ring warms to gold as it lifts.

shadows.name: banner-rest
shadows.purpose: A promotional banner at rest on a paper-2 band. Framed artwork is seated, unlike a card.

shadows.name: banner-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover on a LINKED promotional banner only (a.promotion-card), paired with translateY(-5px).

shadows.name: hero-banner-featured
shadows.purpose: The first hero banner (.is-featured): a gold halo over the hero photograph, brightening to 24% on hover.

shadows.name: tile-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover on a dark photographic tile, paired with translateY(-6px) scale(1.025).

shadows.name: glass-panel
shadows.purpose: Cards over photography, with backdrop-filter: blur(18px). Never on a paper band.

shadows.name: glass-chrome
shadows.purpose: The fixed header over the home hero, with backdrop-filter: blur(28px).

shadows.name: media-seat
shadows.purpose: Large media laid on paper - the product gallery, Sobre's hero visual, the map stage. 7-15% at 18-70px blur.

shadows.name: panel-seat
shadows.purpose: The spec panel and paper step cards: a softer hairline for panels too large to read as a printed card.

shadows.name: bottom-sheet
shadows.purpose: The mobile filter sheet. Cast upward, because the sheet comes from below.

shadows.name: field-focus-glow
shadows.purpose: The only diffuse gold in the system, at 12% opacity, blooming outside a focused field.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The Press Rule: every pressable thing scales to .96 on :active. The system's tactile signature.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background state changes on buttons, links and chips (150-180ms).

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Hover lift on cards, tiles and banners, carousel motion, bottom-sheet slide (200-260ms).

motion.name: image-scale
motion.purpose: Image scaling inside a fixed frame on hover, <= 1.06. Framed banner artwork runs 650ms.

motion.name: entrance
motion.purpose: The one animated moment per page (lm-sobe, 14px rise + fade), staggered 80ms to a 240ms ceiling, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: marquee
motion.purpose: The brand strip: a doubled track translated -50%, paused on hover. Declared in globals.css but the component is unmounted legacy.

narrative.overview:
LM sells things that are measured, fabricated and installed — a window profile, a tempered pane, a pergola span. The site is built in that same grammar. Information is set the way a spec sheet is set: ruled rows, a label on the left, a value on the right, numbers in tabular figures. Nothing is presented as a claim when it can be presented as a measurement. The visitor is meant to read the company the way they'd read the section drawing of an aluminium frame.

Materially the world is two substances. **Paper** — a warm off-white with a second, slightly deeper tone under it — carries everything that must be read: catalogue, prose, tables, forms, the product page. **Ink** — a near-black warm brown — carries everything that must be felt: the hero, the closing call, the footer, the band that shows work. Photography lives only on ink or behind glass, never floating on paper. Gold is the third material and it is used like brass hardware: a 5px dot, a 2px underline, a numbered marker, one button. It is never a surface.

Density is editorial, not dashboard. Bands run 56–90px of vertical air; prose is capped by a `ch` measure so a line never outruns the eye; headings carry hard negative tracking while uppercase labels open wide. One thing has been added to that grammar since the first pass and it is worth naming: **CMS artwork**. Promotional banners are finished PNGs from the panel, and the design system's job for them is to be a frame and nothing else — a fixed aspect ratio, a radius, a hover. The page does not compose type over the art, so the art can be whatever the panel makes it without the system fighting it.
keyCharacteristics: Two substances only — warm paper for reading, warm ink for feeling — alternating as full-bleed bands.
Gold as hardware: dots, underlines, markers, numerals, one button. Never a field.
Data set as ruled lists with tabular numerals, not as cards.
Hairlines at rest; shadow and lift are responses to the pointer, never a resting state.
Glass (blur + inset highlight) exists, but only over photography or ink.
CMS artwork is framed, never overlaid — the frame carries the geometry, the art carries the message.
One serif moment and one animated moment per page. Both are ceilings.

rules.name: The Hardware Rule
rules.body: Gold is hardware, not paint. It may be a dot, a rule, a marker, a numeral, an icon, an underline or one button — it may not be a background wider than a button. If a comp has a gold panel, the panel is wrong. (The two sanctioned exceptions are both small and both deliberate: the 44px pin disc on the map card, and the 12%-opacity focus glow on a field.)

rules.name: The Two Substances Rule
rules.body: A surface is paper or it is ink. There is no third background colour and no gradient between them. Paper 2 and Tinta Profunda are not new substances; they are the same two materials one step apart, used only to keep two same-substance bands from fusing.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral in this system is warm. If a new value reads cool or grey next to Papel, it is not from this world — including Tailwind's `neutral-*` scale, which is the legacy register (see Do's and Don'ts).

rules.name: The Alternating Card Rule
rules.body: In a row of three or four sibling cards, exactly one is inverted to ink and the rest are paper — `nth-child(2)` in the product-detail process row, Sobre's capacidades and método; `first-child` in Localização's cobertura. The inversion is the rhythm; two inverted cards in a row is out of world.

rules.name: The Tracking Follows Size Rule
rules.body: Tracking is a function of size and runs monotonically: -.045 to -.052em at display, -.04em at headline, -.02 to -.035em at title, normal at body, then *positive* — .08em to .16em — the moment type goes uppercase and under 13px. A 44px heading at normal tracking, or an 11px uppercase label at normal tracking, are both immediately wrong.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Every text block declares a cap in `ch`, not in pixels: 12–19ch for headings, 48–68ch for prose. A paragraph without a measure cap is unfinished. (The one place the cap is on the *element* rather than the text is the breadcrumb's current page: 42ch desktop, 22ch mobile, with an ellipsis.)

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif appears at most once per page, on a number or a date. It never sets a heading, never sets prose, and never appears twice on one surface.

rules.name: The Balance/Pretty Rule
rules.body: Headings take `text-wrap: balance`; prose takes `text-wrap: pretty`. Both are applied on every heading and paragraph in the system, without exception.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: A page is a stack of full-bleed bands, each one substance, and the container never carries a background of its own. If you need a colour change, you need a new band.

rules.name: The Closing Ink Rule
rules.body: A page ends on ink. In practice this is the site footer, which is ink on every page; two surfaces additionally close their own content on an ink band immediately above it — Sobre on `sobre-cta` and Produto on `product-detail__units`. Home's contact band and Localização's visita band close on paper and lean on the footer alone. Prefer the explicit ink close on a new surface that carries a primary action.

rules.name: The No Empty Half Rule
rules.body: When a two-column band loses its evidence half — no map, no photo, no image in the CMS — the band collapses to one column and the reading column widens (the `is-solo` modifier, live on `location-visit__grid`). It never ships with half a section blank. This is a layout obligation, not a nicety: content is CMS-driven and the empty case is the normal case.

rules.name: The Frame-Not-Canvas Rule
rules.body: A CMS-supplied banner is framed, never composed on. The system supplies the aspect ratio, radius, ring, hover and focus; the artwork supplies everything inside. No heading, kicker, gradient scrim or button is laid over promotional artwork — if a message needs type, it belongs in the art or in a real band.

rules.name: The Hairline-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: On paper, a *card* at rest is separated by a 1px line and a half-step of tone. Shadow at rest is reserved for large media objects, framed artwork, and things that genuinely float (the bottom sheet, the glass chrome). A resting drop shadow under a paper *card* is still out of world.

rules.name: The Glass Needs Ground Rule
rules.body: `backdrop-filter` is only legitimate where there is something to blur: over photography, over ink, or over a map. Glass on a paper band is a defect, not a variant.

rules.name: The Radius Follows Area Rule
rules.body: A 16px radius on a 48px control, or a 9px radius on a 500px panel, both read as mistakes. Pick from the ladder by the size of the thing.

rules.name: The Pill For Words Rule
rules.body: Anything that contains a word and can be pressed is a pill (999px). Anything that contains only a mark is a circle. There is no in-between rounded rectangle for actions — the one exception is the 56px mobile filter trigger and the sidebar's utility buttons, which are square-ish (10–18px) because they hold an icon inside a grid of fields, not a word inside a row of actions.

rules.name: The Aspect Ratio Rule
rules.body: Any container that receives an unknown image declares an `aspect-ratio` (or a fixed height) and clips. A grid of artwork whose heights are set by the artwork will never align, and CMS art is by definition unknown.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: Every pressable thing scales to `.96` on `:active` over 100ms — buttons, filter chips, cards, thumbnails, sheet controls, linked banners. It is the system's single tactile signature and it is applied without exception. (The band banner presses to `translateY(-2px) scale(.995)` instead, because it is already lifted when pressed.)

rules.name: The One Animated Moment Rule
rules.body: A page gets one entrance animation and no more. It is `lm-sobe` (14px rise + fade, 620ms) staggered in 80ms steps to a 240ms ceiling, currently on Sobre's stat trio and Localização's coverage cards. Both live inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` — opt-in, so motion is never the default. A global `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block additionally clamps every animation and transition in the build to .01ms and disables smooth scrolling.

rules.name: The Hover Is A Bonus Rule
rules.body: `@media (hover: none)` strips every hover transform and shadow. Any state that only exists on hover must have a rest state that already reads — which is why active filters invert their fill, badges are always visible, and arrow discs are drawn at rest.

dos: **Do** compose a new page as a stack of full-bleed bands, alternating substance, and close a surface carrying a primary action on an ink band.
**Do** wrap every band's content in `.lm-container` and let the band's background run full-bleed. One container, no nested max-widths.
**Do** cap every text block with a `ch` measure — 12–19ch headings, 48–68ch prose — and set `text-wrap: balance` on headings, `pretty` on paragraphs.
**Do** set anything with a label and a value as a ruled list with tabular numerals: `dt` muted, `dd` full-contrast and right-aligned, rows divided by a 1px rule.
**Do** use `.button` plus a variant for every action, and pick the variant by ground: gold on paper or ink, creme over photography, dark for the secondary.
**Do** give any container that receives a CMS image a fixed `aspect-ratio` (or height) and `overflow: hidden`, and frame the artwork rather than composing type over it.
**Do** scope hover, lift, press and focus styles to `a.` (or the interactive element) when a component can render inert, so a decorative instance does not advertise an interaction it does not have.
**Do** centre a header-style nav with equal `1fr` side columns rather than by margin, and take any element that would push the centre out of flow.
**Do** let a horizontal trail of items scroll rather than wrap when wrapping would change the height of a fixed band.
**Do** draw new icons as 24-box SVG at `stroke-width: 1.7` with round caps and joins, `fill: none`, `stroke: currentColor`.
**Do** give a two-column band an `is-solo` collapse for when its evidence half has no CMS content.
**Do** hold hover lift within `translateY(-5px … -6px)` and scale ≤ 1.035, and make sure the rest state still reads when `@media (hover: none)` strips it.
**Do** put every entrance animation behind `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, and keep it to one moment per page.
**Do** give every new interactive element a ≥44px target and a visible gold focus ring.
donts: **Don't** introduce a colour outside the palette above. If a comp needs a new hue, it needs a new argument first.
**Don't** fill a surface with gold. Gold is a dot, a rule, a marker, a numeral, an icon or one button; the only diffuse gold in the system is a 12%-opacity focus glow and the 44px map pin.
**Don't** lay type, a scrim or a button over CMS artwork. The frame is the system's contribution; the art is the client's.

**Don't** write a new surface in Tailwind's `neutral-*` utilities. `/solucoes`, `/trabalhos`, `ProdutoCard`, `ProjetoBloco`, `SecaoTrabalhos` and `FaixaDeMarcas` are still in that generic register (`max-w-6xl`, `text-neutral-600`, `border-neutral-300`) and read as a different product — that is **legacy drift to be migrated onto the design system, not a second sanctioned style**. The design system is `globals.css`; the surfaces that speak it are Home, Catálogo, Produto, Sobre and Localização. (The `bg-white text-neutral-900` on `<body>` in the frontend layout is the same holdover.)
**Don't** put glass on a paper band, or a resting drop shadow under a paper *card*. On paper, a card at rest is a hairline; only large media and framed artwork are seated with a shadow.
**Don't** reach for Instrument Serif more than once on a page, and never for a heading or for prose.
**Don't** add a fourth breakpoint. The system is 1100 / 800 / 520 plus the two behavioural queries; a new surface that needs a fifth column count is over-specified.
**Don't** add an eyebrow to a band that already carries a categorising label. It is an existing device in this build, not a required section-opener — a heading that stands alone is finished.
**Don't** signal state with colour alone; add a fill inversion, an underline, a ring or a weight change.

**Don't** carry navigation history in the URL. The product page states its position with breadcrumbs; a `?voltar=` style parameter dirties the address, changes with the referrer, and was removed for exactly that reason.

**Don't** reference a custom property that isn't declared in `:root`. The 800px block still calls `var(--lm-gray-600)` and `var(--lm-gold-500)`, neither of which exists — the home mobile search's clear button therefore loses its colour and its focus ring. That is a bug in the build, not a token; new code must not copy it.

**Don't** leave animation rules pointed at a class the markup no longer renders. The reduced-motion block still staggers `.local-rota__lista`, a route-spine component the Localização redesign removed; it is dead weight, not a pattern to extend.
**Don't** let a card's height float with its copy in a grid. The catalogue card fixes each zone's height so a row aligns; a new card in a grid must do the same.
